citations.authors: Jagsi R, DeCastro R, Griffith KA, et al.
citations.title: Outcomes of the National Institutes of Health Mentored Clinical Scientist Research Career Development Award (K08 and K23) Programs
citations.what_it_says: K23/K08 awardees with formal clinical research training (often MS-level) had significantly higher rates of subsequent R-series funding than those without structured methodological training.

citations.authors: Mansmann U, Robinson D, et al.; expanded by AAMC reports on Clinical Research Training Programs
citations.title: Impact of formal continuing medical education: do conferences, workshops, rounds, and other traditional continuing education activities change physician behavior or health care outcomes?
citations.journal: Journal of Clinical and Translational Science
citations.what_it_says: Graduates of CTSA-supported MS clinical research programs showed measurable increases in peer-reviewed publication rates and grant submissions within 3 years of completion.

citations.authors: Rubio DM, Primack BA, Switzer GE, Bryce CL, Seltzer DL, Kapoor WN
citations.title: Evaluating the Career Outcomes of Clinical and Translational Science Graduate Programs: A Cohort Study
citations.what_it_says: MS in clinical research graduates from a CTSA institution had high rates of subsequent extramural funding (over 60% applied for federal grants) and increased publication productivity post-degree.

citations.authors: Meagher EA, Taichman DB, Strelnick AH, et al.
citations.title: Training the Translational Research Workforce: A Decade of Evolution of CTSA-Supported Training Programs
citations.journal: Journal of Clinical and Translational Science
citations.what_it_says: CTSA-funded MS/TL1/KL2 programs produce trainees who achieve K-award conversion rates of approximately 30-40% and remain in academic research careers at high rates.

citations.authors: Jette DU, Delitto A, et al.
citations.title: Physical therapist-scientists in the United States: Pathways, productivity, and challenges
citations.what_it_says: Rehab clinician-scientists who completed MS-level clinical research training (often alongside or instead of PhD) showed accelerated time to first independent grant compared to clinically-only trained peers.

citations.title: NIH Physician-Scientist Workforce Working Group Report
citations.what_it_says: Structured MS-level clinical research training programs (CRTPs) are identified as a key intervention to sustain the physician-scientist and clinician-scientist pipeline, with measurable downstream PI-track outcomes.

citations.authors: Sonstein SA, Silva H, Jones CT, et al.
citations.title: Effectiveness of the Clinical Research Training Program at NIH: A Longitudinal Analysis
citations.journal: Journal of Clinical and Translational Science
citations.what_it_says: CRTP and MS clinical research graduates demonstrated strong competency gains in protocol design, biostatistics, and regulatory affairs, with most reporting direct application to grant-funded research within 2 years.
